paragraphs: A backdoored model can behave normally on ordinary inputs while producing an attacker’s intended behavior when a trigger appears. This paper studies how to detect suspicious inputs when the model is being used. It first gives a common mathematical formulation that covers several existing inference-stage defenses, making their objectives and limitations easier to analyze together.

The framework provides guarantees on the false positive rate: how often a clean input is incorrectly flagged. Under classical learning scenarios, the authors derive the detection rule with the greatest power at a specified false positive rate. This makes the trade-off explicit: catching more triggered inputs must be considered alongside the cost of rejecting legitimate ones.

The authors then use that theoretical rule to motivate a practical detector based on internal representations of backdoored deep networks. Evaluations cover 14 attacks across vision and language benchmarks and support the theoretical analysis. The abstract reports substantial improvements over existing defenses, including against advanced adaptive attacks. The optimality statement applies to the analyzed scenarios, while the deep-network implementation is supported by these experiments.
neurips-2023-a-unified-detection-framewo.tldr: A unified backdoor-detection framework controls false alarms and motivates a practical detector that performs strongly across vision and language attacks.

paragraphs: Sequential predictors receive examples over time, and methods built for ordinary random data can fail when an adversary inserts unusual examples with correct labels. Treating every example as adversarial, however, can produce overly pessimistic guarantees. This paper introduces an intermediate setting that permits the learner to abstain without cost on adversarial examples.

The central result assumes that the learner knows the marginal distribution of ordinary, non-adversarial inputs. Under this assumption, the authors construct a learner whose error scales with the hypothesis class’s VC dimension, a complexity measure associated with stochastic learning. This replaces dependence on the Littlestone dimension that characterizes the fully adversarial setting, showing how abstention can change the relevant difficulty of sequential prediction.

The paper also constructs learners that do not need access to that marginal distribution for two specific cases: classes with VC dimension one and axis-aligned rectangles. A new measure of uncertainty for VC classes supports the analysis. Together, the results establish conditional guarantees for resisting adversarial insertions while retaining a complexity dependence closer to ordinary statistical learning.
neurips-2023-adversarial-resilience-in-s.tldr: Allowing abstention yields stronger sequential-prediction guarantees under adversarial insertions, with distributional assumptions relaxed for specific hypothesis classes.

paragraphs: Shopping-session models use a customer’s recent interactions to predict what they will do next. Research on these models depends on datasets that represent enough products, attributes, and shopping behaviors. Amazon-M2 addresses limitations in existing session datasets by collecting millions of sessions across six locales, with product languages including English, German, Japanese, French, Italian, and Spanish.

The paper organizes evaluation around three tasks. Next-product recommendation asks which item a shopper will interact with next. A second recommendation task introduces domain shifts, making changes between data settings part of the challenge. The third task asks a model to generate the next product’s title, extending the dataset’s use from choosing products to producing product-related text.

The authors benchmark a range of algorithms on these tasks and use the resource to support a public competition that attracted thousands of users and submissions. The contribution is a shared basis for studying recommendations and text generation across languages and locales. The abstract presents improved personalization as a potential benefit of the dataset, rather than a guaranteed outcome of using it.
neurips-2023-amazon-m2-a-multilingual-mu.tldr: Amazon-M2 provides millions of shopping sessions across six locales for benchmarking multilingual recommendation and product-title generation.

paragraphs: Detecting another aircraft in an image is only one part of a vision-based collision-avoidance system. A useful benchmark must also expose changes in detection performance across environmental conditions and connect perception to the eventual avoidance task. AVOIDDS combines a labeled image dataset, an interface for targeted evaluation, and an integrated simulator to support that broader assessment.

The dataset contains 72,000 photorealistic images of intruder aircraft. Its variation includes lighting, weather, relative aircraft geometry, and geographic location. Researchers can evaluate a trained detector on selected portions of the dataset to examine how its performance changes with these conditions. This allows environmental differences to be investigated directly instead of being hidden inside a single aggregate result.

The closed-loop simulator evaluates trained models as part of the downstream detect-and-avoid process. It therefore complements image-level assessment with testing tied to collision avoidance. The paper’s stated contribution is this benchmark infrastructure for studying robustness in a safety-critical application. It supplies a way to investigate system behavior, rather than claiming that any particular detector has already achieved robust avoidance.
neurips-2023-avoidds-aircraft-vision-bas.tldr: AVOIDDS links aircraft detection under varied conditions to closed-loop collision-avoidance evaluation.

paragraphs: This paper studies collaboration among agents that each observe a different subset of the available features. Such differences can arise when sensors collect information at different resolutions. The objective is to coordinate learning so that each agent obtains a strong least-squares estimator, despite having only a partial view of the features.

The proposed semi-supervised procedure, Collab, has three stages: agents train locally, their results are aggregated, and information is distributed back to them. Labeled examples do not need to be communicated. This makes the procedure useful when those examples cannot be accessed centrally and reduces the communication burden associated with sharing them.

The main theoretical result says that Collab is nearly optimal in an asymptotic, local-minimax sense, even compared with estimators allowed to exchange labeled data, including imputation methods. The qualification matters: this is a specific statistical optimality statement, not a claim of best performance in every finite dataset. The authors also test Collab on US Census data and discuss extensions involving non-Gaussian features, nonlinear models, and federated learning.
neurips-2023-collaboratively-learning-li.tldr: Collab coordinates linear estimation across agents with different feature subsets without exchanging labeled data, while achieving a qualified near-optimality guarantee.

paragraphs: Combinatorial optimization involves choosing among many possible arrangements, such as routes or schedules. Reinforcement learning can learn rules for constructing these solutions, but finding strong solutions also depends on how those rules are explored when a new problem arrives. The paper identifies two common approaches: repeatedly sampling from one policy, which can restrict search diversity, and fine-tuning a policy for each instance, which can be computationally expensive.

COMPASS builds the needs of this later search into pre-training. It represents a collection of diverse, specialized policies controlled by a continuous latent space. Searching that space provides a way to explore different solution-building behaviors. The central idea is that training should prepare a useful range of policies for search, so adaptation to an instance becomes part of how the learned solver is used.

The authors evaluate COMPASS on travelling salesman, capacitated vehicle routing, and job-shop scheduling problems. They report better performance than state-of-the-art approaches on 9 of 11 standard benchmark tasks. They also report stronger generalization across 18 procedurally transformed instance distributions, outperforming every comparison approach there. These findings support the value of preparing policy diversity during training for effective search on the evaluated problems.
neurips-2023-combinatorial-optimization-.tldr: COMPASS trains diverse policies organized by a continuous latent space, enabling search that outperforms comparison approaches on most tested benchmarks and all tested transformed distributions.

paragraphs: Prediction intervals express uncertainty by giving a range intended to contain the true outcome. Equal overall coverage across demographic groups can still conceal differences among people with similar outcomes. This paper introduces Equal Opportunity of Coverage, or EOC, to make that finer comparison part of uncertainty-aware fairness in regression.

EOC seeks similar coverage rates for different groups when their outcomes are similar, while keeping population-wide coverage at a predetermined level. The intervals should also remain narrow enough to be useful. These goals connect fairness to both reliability and informativeness: matching group coverage alone does not address whether the population target is met or whether the reported ranges are excessively broad.

The authors propose Binned Fair Quantile Regression, a distribution-free post-processing method applicable to trained prediction models. It uses a held-out calibration set to bound deviations from EOC, then uses conformal prediction to maintain EOC on test data while optimizing interval width. Experiments demonstrate improved EOC. The reported contribution is a practical method for improving this fairness criterion while managing the competing need for informative prediction intervals.
neurips-2023-equal-opportunity-of-covera.tldr: Equal Opportunity of Coverage measures interval fairness among groups with similar outcomes, and BFQR improves it through calibration and conformal prediction.

paragraphs: Neural architecture search asks how to design a network that performs well without relying entirely on manual architecture choices. This paper uses code-generating language models inside an evolutionary search process. The language model serves as an adaptive mechanism for modifying and combining candidate architectures, extending its role beyond producing a design from a single prompt.

EvoPrompting combines evolutionary prompt engineering with soft prompt-tuning. The authors find that prompting alone is insufficient for the architecture-search task they study, whereas this combined procedure consistently discovers diverse, high-performing networks. Its approach ties language-model generation to an ongoing search process, so architecture proposals can benefit from adaptation throughout the search.

On MNIST-1D, EvoPrompting produces convolutional variants that improve accuracy and model size relative to human-designed architectures and naive few-shot prompting. On the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, it discovers graph-network architectures that outperform the stated leading models on 21 of 30 tasks with similar model size. These findings demonstrate successful search across the evaluated settings; the authors also describe the framework as adaptable to tasks beyond network design.
neurips-2023-evoprompting-language-model.tldr: EvoPrompting combines evolutionary search and soft prompt-tuning to make language models effective generators of accurate, efficient neural architectures.

paragraphs: Quality-diversity reinforcement learning aims to produce many successful policies that behave differently. Keeping thousands of separate policies, however, consumes substantial storage and makes it harder to accommodate additional behaviors. This paper asks whether a single generative model can preserve much of an archive’s performance and behavioral range while representing it more compactly.

The proposed method distills the archive into a diffusion model that generates policy parameters. Instead of storing every policy separately, the model represents a source from which policies can be produced. This makes preserving both reward and behavioral coverage central: compressing the archive would be less useful if it retained only a narrow set of successful behaviors.

The authors report thirteenfold compression while recovering 98% of the original rewards and 89% of the original humanoid archive’s coverage. These figures show substantial retention rather than complete preservation. Conditioning the diffusion model also enables flexible selection and sequencing of behaviors, including through language. The resulting model therefore serves both as a compressed representation of the archive and as an interface for choosing behaviors.
neurips-2023-generating-behaviorally-div.tldr: A diffusion model compresses a diverse policy archive thirteenfold while retaining most rewards and behavioral coverage and enabling conditioned behavior selection.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a clothed person in three dimensions from one image is especially difficult when poses are complicated or clothing hangs loosely. The paper attributes weaknesses in existing approaches partly to limited image features and inconsistent ways of querying them. GTA addresses these issues with a transformer architecture designed to connect global image information with a structured three-dimensional representation.

A Vision Transformer first extracts features that capture relationships across the image. A decoder then uses cross-attention and learned queries to produce tri-plane features, representing three-dimensional information across three planes. The method also combines spatial queries with queries enhanced by a human-body prior. This fusion brings together information about location and prior knowledge of body structure.

Experiments on CAPE and THuman2.0 show improvements over the compared state-of-the-art methods in both reconstructed geometry and texture. The reported results include robustness to challenging poses and loose clothing, alongside higher-resolution textures. The approach matters because it coordinates global visual context, three-dimensional features, and body knowledge within one reconstruction system, with empirical support for those difficult image conditions.
neurips-2023-global-correlated-3d-decoup.tldr: GTA combines global image features, tri-plane decoding, and body priors to improve single-image reconstruction of clothed human avatars.

paragraphs: Comparing two point clouds can involve finding a correspondence that preserves distances between pairs of points as closely as possible. The Gromov-Wasserstein problem formalizes this structural comparison and can measure similarity between shapes or formations. Its quadratic assignment formulation is generally computationally intractable, even when the number of points is relatively small.

This paper exploits additional structure when the points lie in low-dimensional Euclidean spaces and the discrepancy uses the squared Euclidean norm. The authors express the problem as a low-rank concave quadratic optimization and reformulate it over a low-dimensional domain. That change makes the geometric structure central to the computation rather than treating the task as an unrestricted quadratic assignment problem.

The resulting framework scales well with the number of points and can find global solutions for problems containing thousands of points. The authors compare computational complexity with state-of-the-art approaches on synthetic problems and apply the method to a near-symmetrical problem relevant to computational biology. The global-solution capability is established for the structured setting studied, preserving the importance of low dimensionality and the specified discrepancy.
neurips-2023-globally-solving-the-gromov.tldr: A low-dimensional reformulation enables global Gromov-Wasserstein solutions for large point clouds in the paper’s structured Euclidean setting.

paragraphs: Collaborative learning needs participants to contribute useful information, but valuing contributions without considering privacy can overlook a major cost of participation. This paper builds differential privacy into the incentive mechanism. Each participant chooses a required privacy guarantee and perturbs a sufficient statistic, a summary of data relevant to the model, accordingly.

A mediator values each perturbed summary through Bayesian surprise: how much it changes beliefs about model parameters. This creates a privacy-valuation trade-off. Stronger privacy protection that makes a contribution less informative also reduces its assessed value, discouraging choices that excessively diminish the usefulness of the combined model. Participants can therefore express privacy requirements within the same process that evaluates their contributions.

Rewards take the form of different posterior samples of model parameters for different participants. The authors state that these rewards satisfy existing incentive properties such as fairness while preserving differential privacy and remaining highly similar to the full coalition’s posterior. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support the approach’s effectiveness and practicality. The contribution links privacy choices, information value, and access to learned model knowledge in one collaborative mechanism.
neurips-2023-incentives-in-private-colla.tldr: A collaborative-learning mechanism connects participants’ privacy choices to contribution value and rewards them with privacy-preserving posterior samples.

paragraphs: Organizations can benefit from learning together while still competing over the performance of their individual models. That competition may reward misleading updates that damage other participants’ results. This paper models such interactions as a game, making the incentives behind dishonest communication an explicit part of the learning problem.

The theoretical analysis covers single-round mean estimation and multi-round stochastic gradient descent on strongly convex objectives. For a natural class of available actions, the authors show that rational clients have incentives to manipulate updates strongly enough to prevent learning. They then design mechanisms that encourage honest communication and provide learning quality comparable to full cooperation within the studied framework.

The authors also demonstrate their incentive scheme on a standard non-convex federated-learning benchmark. This experiment extends the empirical evaluation beyond the strongly convex setting of the stated multi-round analysis. The broader lesson is that understanding why participants might interfere can help construct robust collaboration rules. Here, honesty is encouraged through the structure of the interaction, and the guarantees depend on the modeled incentives and actions.
neurips-2023-incentivizing-honesty-among.tldr: Game-theoretic mechanisms encourage competing learners to communicate honestly and recover learning quality comparable to full cooperation in the analyzed settings.

paragraphs: Sample complexity describes how much data is needed to learn successfully. This paper studies that question for linear predictors that output vectors and are represented by matrices, then extends the investigation to neural networks. The focus is on bounds that do not directly depend on model size, using distance from a fixed reference matrix to control the parameter class.

Specifically, the analysis constrains the Frobenius norm of the difference between the learned parameters and a reference matrix W0. This measures overall parameter displacement from the reference. The authors show that the resulting sample-complexity behavior can differ surprisingly from the familiar case of linear predictors with a single scalar output, so intuition from that simpler setting does not transfer straightforwardly.

These results lead to new bounds for feed-forward neural networks and address open questions in the literature. The paper also identifies a convex linear prediction problem that is provably learnable without uniform convergence, the usual requirement that empirical performance approximate population performance across a whole predictor class. This establishes a concrete separation between successful learning and that particular route to proving it.
neurips-2023-initialization-dependent-sa.tldr: Reference-dependent sample-complexity bounds reveal unexpected behavior in vector-valued prediction and a convex learning problem learnable without uniform convergence.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning trains decision-making policies from previously collected data without gathering new experience from the environment. Small datasets with narrow coverage can make this difficult. This paper uses time-reversal symmetry in system dynamics to extract more useful structure from limited data and to assess samples beyond the observed distribution.

Its Time-reversal symmetry enforced Dynamics Model links forward and reverse dynamics in a learned latent representation. Consistency between these directions serves two purposes: it supports useful representations from small datasets and supplies a reliability measure for out-of-distribution samples. The authors build TSRL around these properties, using less conservative policy constraints and data augmentation within the latent space.

The reported experiments show strong performance on reduced benchmark datasets containing as little as 1% of the original samples. TSRL significantly outperforms the compared recent offline reinforcement-learning algorithms in data efficiency and generalizability. These findings support the method’s use of dynamical consistency as both a learning signal and a guide for augmentation, with the performance claim tied to the evaluated small-data benchmarks.
neurips-2023-look-beneath-the-surface-ex.tldr: TSRL uses consistency between forward and reverse latent dynamics to improve offline reinforcement learning from small datasets.

paragraphs: A multi-armed bandit learner repeatedly chooses among options while learning about their rewards. In applications such as recommendation and advertising, those rewards can change over time in structured ways. This paper introduces a non-stationary bandit framework with autoregressive rewards, allowing temporal dependence to be part of the model rather than treating change as unstructured.

The proposed algorithm combines alternation and restarting. Alternation uses temporal dependencies to adjust the balance between exploring uncertain options and exploiting currently useful ones. Restarting discards information that has become outdated. Together, these mechanisms address two consequences of changing rewards: recent observations can be informative about what comes next, while sufficiently old observations can lose their relevance.

The authors establish a regret upper bound that nearly matches a lower bound, measuring performance against a robust dynamic benchmark. This provides a near-matching theoretical characterization within the proposed framework. A case study on tourism demand prediction also demonstrates the algorithm’s effectiveness and supports the applicability of the techniques to more complex, rapidly changing time series.
neurips-2023-non-stationary-bandits-with.tldr: An autoregressive bandit framework combines adaptive exploration and restarting to exploit temporal structure while discarding outdated information.

paragraphs: Machine teaching studies how a teacher can choose examples that help a learner acquire a target concept more quickly. Much of this work considers one learner at a time. This paper instead studies iterative teaching for multiple learners simultaneously, motivated by instructional settings where a teacher works with several students.

The proposed framework, MINT, lets each learner pursue a scalar-valued target model while expressing the combined teaching problem through a vector-valued target. Mathematically, it extends the reproducing kernel Hilbert space used for individual learners to a vector-valued space. This formulation puts the learners into one joint teaching problem rather than simply repeating a separate teaching procedure for each of them.

The authors show significant teaching speed-ups over repeated single-learner teaching, particularly when learners can communicate with one another. Extensive experiments also support the framework’s practicality and efficiency. The result gives a formal way to study coordinated instruction and indicates that communication between learners can be especially valuable within this setting. The stated evidence concerns the proposed learning framework and its experiments.
neurips-2023-nonparametric-teaching-for-.tldr: MINT formulates teaching multiple learners as a joint vector-valued problem and achieves speed-ups, especially when learners communicate.

paragraphs: High-fidelity head-avatar research needs detailed observations of people across viewpoints, appearances, and motion. Existing public datasets can restrict both the range of people represented and the tasks researchers can study. RenderMe-360 provides a large collection of dynamic human-head assets intended to support several directions of avatar research within one resource.

The dataset includes more than 243 million complete head frames and over 800,000 video sequences from 500 identities. Capture uses 60 synchronized 2K cameras covering 360 degrees at 30 frames per second. Subjects vary in appearance and background, and perform expressions and head rotations. Annotations range from camera parameters and background matting to scans, facial landmarks, fitted face models, and text descriptions.

The authors benchmark 16 state-of-the-art methods across five tasks: novel-view synthesis, novel-expression synthesis, hair rendering, hair editing, and talking-head generation. These experiments reveal strengths and weaknesses of existing methods. The resource’s contribution is therefore both broader training material and a common evaluation setting spanning multiple aspects of head-avatar creation, rather than a single new avatar-generation algorithm.
neurips-2023-renderme-360-a-large-digita.tldr: RenderMe-360 supplies extensive multi-view head recordings, rich annotations, and benchmarks across five avatar-generation tasks.

paragraphs: Neural networks can rely on simple predictive features even when more complex features could support greater robustness. This paper makes that simplicity bias mathematically precise by describing a network that depends mainly on a low-dimensional projection of its input. That definition enables analysis beyond examples where features are easy to specify by hand.

For one-hidden-layer networks in the infinite-width regime, the authors show that linearly separable data can lead the network to rely primarily on a one-dimensional separating subspace. This happens even with arbitrarily many more complex features available that could yield a substantially more robust classifier. The theoretical statement is tied to the network regime and data condition studied.

Experiments on ImageNet and Waterbirds-Landbirds also find models whose predictions depend on low-dimensional input projections, providing empirical evidence of simplicity bias on real datasets. The authors then train an ensemble whose successive models use features earlier models did not use. This encourages diversity and produces substantially greater robustness to Gaussian noise, connecting the analysis of restricted feature use to a concrete intervention.
neurips-2023-simplicity-bias-in-1-hidden.tldr: The paper formalizes simplicity bias through low-dimensional input dependence and uses feature-diverse ensembles to improve robustness to Gaussian noise.

paragraphs: Navigation maps can lack detail, contain errors, and require substantial effort to maintain. SNAP explores building richer two-dimensional maps directly from ground-level and overhead imagery. Its neural maps are learned representations intended to support both locating images and understanding the scenes they depict.

Training aligns maps produced from different inputs, using camera poses as the only supervision across tens of millions of StreetView images. This encourages different views to produce compatible map representations. Although semantic labels are not supplied explicitly, the learned maps capture high-level meaning alongside geometry and visual appearance. The supervision is therefore limited in type, rather than absent altogether.

The authors report a large improvement over the state of the art in visual localization, including difficult image queries that traditional methods cannot resolve. The learned representations also provide effective pre-training for semantic scene understanding with limited data. These findings connect positioning and scene interpretation through one mapping approach, while cheaper creation of more detailed maps remains a potential application described by the authors.
neurips-2023-snap-self-supervised-neural.tldr: SNAP learns neural maps from imagery using camera-pose supervision, improving visual localization and supporting data-efficient semantic understanding.

paragraphs: Weather forecasting two to six weeks ahead is valuable for planning resources and adapting to climate conditions, but it is a difficult prediction horizon. Forecast targets depend on complicated relationships between local weather and global climate variables. Machine learning has shown promise, yet assembling suitable training data requires considerable work across sources, formats, and spatial and temporal resolutions.

SubseasonalClimateUSA provides a curated dataset for training and comparing subseasonal forecasting models in the United States. Its contribution is to streamline the data preparation that otherwise accompanies model development. Bringing the relevant material into a shared resource makes it easier to investigate forecasting methods using a common basis for evaluation.

The authors benchmark operational dynamical models, classical meteorological baselines, and ten machine-learning and deep-learning methods from the literature. Their results suggest simple, effective ways to improve the accuracy of current operational models. The abstract also describes the dataset as regularly updated and available through a Python package. The paper thus combines data infrastructure with comparative evidence intended to guide further forecasting research.
neurips-2023-subseasonalclimateusa-a-dat.tldr: SubseasonalClimateUSA streamlines US weather forecasting research two to six weeks ahead and benchmarks methods for improving operational forecasts.

paragraphs: Sequential observations can mix together hidden variables whose causal influences unfold over time. Recovering those variables becomes harder when the data-generating process changes. Existing approaches to this nonstationary setting may rely on observed labels or domain indicators, or impose simplified hidden dynamics. This paper investigates recovery using the measured sequence without those auxiliary observations.

The theoretical analysis uses the Markov assumption for processes with time-delayed causal relationships. Under conditions described as mild, the authors show that independent latent components can be recovered from nonlinear mixtures up to permutation and component-wise transformation. That qualification defines the recovery guarantee: the components can be reordered and individually transformed, so exact recovery in their original coordinates is not claimed.

The proposed NCTRL framework estimates time-delayed latent variables and identifies their relationships from sequential data alone. Empirical evaluations show reliable identification of delayed causal influences and substantial improvements over compared methods that inadequately exploit nonstationarity and fail to distinguish distribution shifts. The contribution combines a conditional identifiability result with an estimation method that uses changing temporal structure.
neurips-2023-temporally-disentangled-rep.tldr: NCTRL recovers temporally related latent variables under unknown nonstationarity, supported by conditional identifiability guarantees and empirical results.

paragraphs: Evaluating a generative model requires judging both sample quality and the range of outputs it produces. Many metrics depend on estimating the support of sample features: the regions occupied by the underlying distributions. This paper argues that unreliable support estimates can undermine the evaluation itself, causing existing metrics to misjudge quality or produce inconsistent results.

Topological Precision and Recall, or TopP&R, makes support estimation the central design concern. It retains features that are significant both topologically and statistically at a specified confidence level. The aim is to base fidelity and diversity assessment on supported structure in the samples, reducing the influence of unreliable features in the estimated distributions.

The authors provide theoretical and experimental findings supporting robust evaluation and statistical consistency under noise conditions. Their results show that TopP&R captures the direction of changes in sample quality in the presence of outliers and non-IID perturbations, where compared methods produce inaccurate support estimates. This connects the reliability of a generative-model score to the quality of the distributional structure used to calculate it.
neurips-2023-topp-r-robust-support-estim.tldr: TopP&R improves generative-model evaluation by estimating distribution supports robustly using topological and statistical significance.

paragraphs: Controlling generated video requires specifying both what appears and how it changes across frames. That is difficult because motion varies widely and neighboring frames must remain coherent. VideoComposer addresses this through compositional generation, allowing text, spatial information, and temporal information to jointly guide the synthesized video.

The method uses motion vectors from compressed video as an explicit signal for temporal dynamics. It also introduces a Spatio-Temporal Condition encoder that provides a shared interface for sequential inputs. This encoder incorporates relationships within and across frames, helping the model use temporal conditions more effectively and improve consistency between generated frames.

Experimental results suggest that VideoComposer can control spatial and temporal patterns simultaneously through several input forms, including text descriptions, sketch sequences, reference videos, and hand-crafted motions. The contribution is a unified way to combine these kinds of control in video synthesis. Its findings support flexible motion guidance in the evaluated settings, connecting user-supplied conditions to both visual content and how that content develops over time.
neurips-2023-videocomposer-compositional.tldr: VideoComposer combines text, spatial cues, and explicit motion signals to guide video content and temporal behavior together.

paragraphs: Autonomous-driving planners need simulation environments that support large-scale testing and meaningful interactions among road users. Waymax is a data-driven simulator built for multi-agent driving scenes. It uses publicly released real-world driving data to initialize scenarios or replay recorded behavior, providing a varied foundation for training and evaluation.

The simulator runs entirely on accelerators such as GPUs and TPUs and supports simulation within the training computation graph. This design makes it suitable for distributed machine-learning workflows. Learned and hard-coded behavior models allow simulated agents to interact during online training and evaluation, complementing the use of recorded scenarios with responsive behavior.

The authors also benchmark imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning algorithms and examine different design decisions through ablation studies. They highlight the usefulness of routes as guidance for planning agents and show that reinforcement learning can overfit to simulated agents. That finding matters when interpreting simulation performance: success can reflect adaptation to the particular agents used in training. Waymax contributes both scalable infrastructure and evidence about choices that shape planning results within it.
neurips-2023-waymax-an-accelerated-data-.tldr: Waymax enables accelerator-based multi-agent driving simulation and benchmarks planning choices, including route guidance and overfitting to simulated agents.
